key_insight: Confinement-controlled synthesis produces highly n-phase-pure 2D lead bromide perovskite powders, enabling band-edge tuning through controlled mixing.
engineering_relevance: Phase-pure powders offer a route to tailored optical absorption and photocurrent response, although solar-cell performance is not demonstrated.
method: Synthesize layered perovskite microcrystals using cesium and butylammonium A-cations.
Characterize optical properties, structure, and composition using spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and energy-dispersive spectroscopy.
Press pure and mixed powders into pellets for spectral and dynamic photocurrent measurements.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports sharp absorption onsets, single narrow UV-blue emission peaks, and composition-dependent spectral and dynamic photocurrent responses.
watch_item: Translation from pressed pellets to practical solar cells remains unproven; the abstract provides no photovoltaic efficiency or operational stability data.
paper_title: Confinement Controlled Phase-Pure 2D Layered Perovskites for Band-Edge Engineering
